tasks.title: Email about photography workshop
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: Read this email from your English teacher, Mrs. Hill, and the notes you have made.

promptBlocks.subject: Photography workshop planning
paragraphs: As you know, our class is helping to plan a photography workshop for local teenagers. We need to decide on the main goal. Should we focus on teaching technical skills like using a camera, or on helping students express their ideas through photos? Which do you think is more important and why?
Also, we need to choose one practical thing to organise. Would you prefer to arrange a visit to a local photography exhibition, or invite a professional photographer to give a talk?
Finally, can you suggest one way to make the workshop affordable for everyone?

promptBlocks.heading: Notes for your reply
listItems: Say which goal you prefer (technical skills OR expressing ideas) and explain why.
Choose a practical thing to organise (exhibition visit OR photographer talk) and give a reason.
Suggest one way to make the workshop affordable.
Ask Mrs. Hill about the date of the workshop.

promptBlocks.text: Write your email to Mrs. Hill using all the notes.

tasks.title: Article about photography workshop
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.heading: Articles wanted!
paragraphs: Our town is planning a photography workshop for teenagers. Do you think this is a good idea? What would you like to learn in a photography workshop?
Write an article answering these questions and we will put it on our town website!

tasks.title: Story about photography workshop
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story.
Your story must begin with this sentence:
"When the programme coordinator opened the camera bag, a memory card fell out with a note attached."
